description:
Problem: the owner requires the local and CI reviews to be literally the same code, differing only where the execution environment forces it. Today CI orchestration lives in about 20 gated steps of .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml (select, scans, isolation, loop, finalize, redact, guard, posts, uploads, dispatch), with if: chains acting as a second decision layer, while the local path re-implements most of it in local.py.

Prior art: the single-job decision record (_project/decisions/oracle-single-review-job-2026-10-25.md) and the existing cli.py subcommands; this item extends them into one entrypoint rather than adding a parallel layer.

Outcome: one driver entrypoint (for example cli.py review) runs a fixed sequence: trusted inputs, plan, classify, pre-scan, harness ensure (pin file), isolation check, attempts, post-scan, finalize and judge, redact, record and post (status, review or comment, retry state), gate dispatch. It runs through an environment adapter interface covering PR context, change source, credential client, classifier key source, isolation capability, scan roots, result sink, state store and harness binary. The CI adapter supplies GitHub event context and sinks. oracle-verdict.yml keeps only environment-forced steps (checkouts, provisioning, tailnet join, App-token mint, artifact upload) and one driver invocation; the sweep job calls a driver subcommand. The reviewer stays self-contained behind this entrypoint and one pinned config, so the planned split into a separate project is a move (owner Q11).

Decision gates:
1. Characterise first: on develop, capture plan, final, status and comment outputs for a fixture matrix (first review, follow-up, carry, dispute, fork, draft, oversize, absence, integrity error, App missing) as golden tests that pass on develop; the refactor must pass them unchanged.
2. Secrets keep their step scoping: the App key appears only after the loop; the classifier key never enters the attempt loop's process tree; the gateway token only in the loop. If the driver must hold a secret in-process, it drops it before attempts; prove with leak tests.
3. Isolation checks stay fail-closed in CI.
4. If any behaviour cannot move without changing outcomes, stop and report (Q10 lifted the 'no CI change' guardrail for the caller, not for behaviour).

Item guardrails: no change to policy, selection, the decision rule, budgets or the gate; no new workflow permissions.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. Never use git stash (refs/stash is shared across worktrees). Commit as Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>, staging explicit paths only; no git add -A, no --no-verify, no SKIP, no agent trailers. Durable text (commits, PR bodies, docs, code) carries no tracker ids, session labels or plan references. Maintained code has no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check). Before publishing run make docs-reference-inventory-check, make doc-contracts-guard and make pr-preflight, and self-review with the code review action, fixing every Critical and Required finding. Publish only with make pr-open: never gh pr create, a raw push-and-open, or a PR-body override line; if make pr-open refuses, stop and report the exact refusal instead of routing around it. Until oracle-omp-pin-single-source-20261026 merges, make pr-open may run only with PATH prefixed by the darwin-arm64 omp 18.12.1 build whose SHA-256 that item records, verified with shasum immediately before use; never any other side-loaded omp. Close out only with oracle SHIP on the exact head, every oracle thread answered (reply naming the fixing SHA, then resolve) and make pr-arm; never raw gh pr merge, a stand-in, an adjudication, or a ruleset or settings change. Never print tokens, keys, or the gateway URL or hostname; never spend model quota outside the review harness. Owner decisions are recorded in context and in the decisions file; a step that would contradict one stops and asks the owner.
